 Knicks vs Bucks Game Notes | November 10, 2026
 November 10, 2026 1:21 PM EST November 10, 2026 7:30 PM ET | Madison Square Garden (New York, NY) | Game 10; Home Game 6
 TV: MSG Networks; Radio: SiriusXM
 This Day in Knicks History 
 November 10, 1971: Knicks acquire Earl “The Pearl” Monroe from Baltimore in exchange for Mike Riordan, Dave Stallworth and cash considerations. Monroe, whose number 15 hangs from The Garden rafters, helped lead the Knicks to the 1973 championship and is seventh on the franchise’s all-time scoring list with 9,679 points. 
 November 10, 1978: Red Holzman ends his retirement to return to the Knicks bench. 
 Learn more about Knicks history. 
 Last Game vs. MIL: 
 Milwaukee (2/27/26) --- The New York Knicks defeated the Milwaukee Bucks, 127-98. Jalen Brunson led New York with 27 points on 64.7-percent shooting, seven rebounds and three assists. OG Anunoby registered 24 points on 80.0-percent shooting, three rebounds, three assists and two steals. Karl-Anthony Towns recorded 17 points, 13 rebounds and one assist. Kevin Porter Jr. led Milwaukee with 11 points, 10 assists, six rebounds, one steal and one block. Myles Turner scored 19 points on 62.5-percent shooting, four rebounds, two assists and one block. Kyle Kuzma netted 17 points on 54.5-percent shooting, four rebounds and two assists. 
 Connections: 
 Knicks forward OG Anunoby and Bucks guard Gary Trent Jr. played together on the Toronto Raptors from 2020-2024… Bucks center Jericho Sims was drafted by the Knicks in the second round of the 2021 NBA Draft and spent four seasons with New York...Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma and Knicks guard Landry Shamet were teammates together on the Washington Wizards for one season (2023-24)...Knicks guard forward Josh Hart and Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma were teammates on the Los Angeles Lakers (2017-2019). 
 Last Game: 
 The New York Knicks defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 109-97. Jalen Brunson led New York with 31 points, nine assists and six rebounds. Karl-Anthony Towns registered 29 points on 52.4-percent shooting, 13 rebounds, three assists and two steals. OG Anunoby added 15 points, six rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Donovan Mitchell led Cleveland with 37 points on 59.1-percent shooting, four rebounds, four assists, two steals and one block. Evan Mobley added 12 points, nine rebounds and five assists. Peyton Watson also contributed 12 points, six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal.
 KAT & CAP COMBINE FOR 60 POINTS IN CLEVELAND:  
 Karl-Anthony Towns recorded 29 points on 52.4-percent shooting, 13 rebounds, three assists and two steals against Cleveland (Nov 7). This marks his 487th career double-double, which ties with Anthony Davis for the seventh most double-doubles amongst active players. Towns has recorded a double-double in nine straight games to start the season, which is tied for the second-longest double-double streak to start a season in franchise history. This also marks Towns’ 81st 20-point double-double as a Knick, which ranks ninth in franchise history. 
 Jalen Brunson recorded 20 points in the first half against Cleveland (Nov 7). This marks his 76th half as a Knick scoring 20+ points, which ranks second in franchise history. Brunson finished with 31 points, nine assists and six rebounds against Cleveland (Nov 7). This marks his 83rd game as a Knick with 30+ points and at least five or more assists, which ranks first in franchise history. This also marks his 104th game as Knick scoring 30+ points, which ranks third in franchise history. It also marks Jalen’s 31st game with 30+ points, five or more assists and five or more rebounds, which ranks fourth all-time in franchise history (Walt Frazier in third with 32). 
 Andre Drummond recorded two steals in the first half against Cleveland (11/7). This marks his 253rd half in his career recording at least two or more steals, which is the most such halves by a center since tracking started (1996-97). 
 Landry Shamet recorded two steals against Cleveland (11/7). This marks his 10th game as Knick recording two or more steals. 
 Miles McBride tied Charlie Ward for the seventh-most three-pointers off the bench in Knicks history (273).
